transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well... I guess I’m here because I just... I don't care about anything anymore. And I mean literally anything. It’s like someone just reached into my head and unplugged the part of me that actually wants to do things or be alive. I used to be so active, you know? I was taking these art classes at the community college—watercolor and acrylics mostly, I was actually getting really good at painting landscapes and mixing colors—but now my supplies are just sitting in the corner collecting dust and I can't even bring myself to look at them. 

And it’s not just the art. I used to host these big board-game nights every other Thursday with my friends, we’d play Settlers of Catan or those really long strategy games for hours, but I haven't answered their texts in weeks. I just don't see the point. Same with hiking. I used to go out on the trails every single weekend, rain or shine, just to be outside. I was even talking about getting back on my old recreational soccer team, the one I played with a few years ago, because I missed running around... but now? Now I just sit in my room. All day. I just sit there on the edge of my bed, staring at the wall or the floor, and I watch the hours go by. I just let everything slip away. It's like I'm watching my whole life disappear from the inside of my bedroom, all the things that used to make me *me*, and I don't even have the energy to care that it's happening. I don't know how it got this bad, I really don't, but I just can't make myself care about a single thing.
Do you still find any pleasure in the things you used to enjoy, or has that completely gone away?

No, it's... it's completely gone. Like I was saying, it's just zero. Zero pleasure. Zero interest. I look at my paints—the watercolors, the expensive brushes I saved up for, the little tubes of acrylics that I used to get so excited about buying at the craft store—and I feel absolutely nothing. It's like looking at a pile of rocks. And the board-game nights... I mean, my friends used to text me all the time, "Hey, when are we playing Catan again? When are we doing the next game night?" and I used to love it. I used to spend hours setting up the snacks and making sure the table was cleared off, but now... I just look at the texts and I can't even type back a single word. It just feels so heavy. 

Even the hiking, which used to be my escape, you know? I'd go up to the state park, take the long trail by the river, and just breathe. I haven't been in months. My hiking boots are just sitting by the door. And the soccer team... I was really, really thinking about calling the old captain. I had the number pulled up on my phone a few times, thinking, "Maybe if I just run around, maybe if I just sweat it out, I'll feel like myself again." But I never called. I couldn't. I just... I don't care. I sit on my bed. I look at the wall. I look at the dust on my art supplies. I see the boots by the door. And I just let it all slip away. It's all just gone. Everything that made me happy is just... empty now.
How long have you been feeling this way?

Well... it's been a really long time. I mean, I remember it starting to get bad, like really bad, around the summer of last year. So, I guess that makes it... what, a year and four months? Yeah, about a year and four months where it's just been this constant, heavy blanket over everything. But honestly, it feels like it's been a lifetime. 

I remember last summer so clearly because that was supposed to be when I finally went back to my art classes. I had signed up for this advanced watercolor technique course at the community college—it was on Tuesday and Thursday evenings, and the instructor was this amazing local artist who I'd been wanting to learn from for years. I had even bought this special cold-pressed paper, the really expensive kind that doesn't warp when it gets wet, and I was so ready. But then... July hit, and it was just like someone flipped a switch. I never went to a single class. I couldn't even make myself drive to the campus. I just sat in my room with the AC running, staring at the blank paper, feeling absolutely nothing. 

And it hasn't let up since. Not for a single day. Fall came, and usually I love the fall—the leaves changing, the crisp air, that's prime hiking season for me. I usually do the Ridge Trail in October because the colors are incredible. But I didn't go once. Then winter, then spring, and now here we are again, and it's just been this endless stretch of... nothing. Sixteen months of just sitting on the edge of my bed, watching the seasons change outside my window and not caring at all. Sixteen months of ignoring texts from my board-game friends. I mean, they don't even text me anymore, really. Why would they? I haven't been a person for a year and four months. It's just been this constant, unrelenting emptiness since last summer, every single day, from the minute I wake up until I finally manage to fall asleep.
Do you ever think that things will never get better for you?

Well... yeah. Honestly, yeah, all the time. It's just... it's like this constant, suffocating weight, you know? Most days, almost every single day, I wake up and before I even open my eyes, I can feel it. It's this heavy, hollow feeling right here in the center of my chest, like someone scooped out everything that makes a person human and just poured lead in there instead. And when I finally do open my eyes and look around my room—at the dust on my easel, at the hiking boots I haven't touched in over a year—it just hits me that this is it. This is all there is. 

I just lie there and think, "What's the point of even getting up?" Because I look ahead, into tomorrow, or next week, or next year, and I don't see anything. I don't see myself painting again, I don't see myself laughing at a board game, I don't see myself running on a soccer field. I just see these four walls. It feels like there is absolutely no future for me beyond the walls of this apartment. Like my whole life has already happened, and now I'm just... existing in the aftermath of it. I try to remember what it felt like to have hope, to look forward to something, like how I used to look forward to that Tuesday night watercolor class, but I can't even grasp the concept of it anymore. It's just this endless, gray tunnel, and I'm stuck right in the middle of it, and I really, truly believe that this is just how it's going to be forever. I don't see how it could possibly ever get better when it's been this dark for so long.
Have you ever thought about harming yourself or wished you were dead?

I... yeah. I have. I mean, it's not like I have this detailed plan with a date circled on a calendar or anything, but... the thoughts are just there. All the time. It's like this constant background noise in my head, just whispering that it would be so much easier if I just... wasn't here anymore. Every night when I finally manage to fall asleep, which is a whole struggle on its own, my last thought before I drift off is always, "I hope I don't wake up tomorrow." I just don't want to wake up. I don't want to open my eyes and face another day of this heavy, suffocating nothingness. It's exhausting. It's just so physically and mentally exhausting to exist like this.

And... well, it actually got really scary a couple of weeks ago. My friend Sarah, she's the one who used to organize the board game nights, she actually came over because I hadn't answered her texts in weeks. She used her spare key—I gave it to her years ago to feed my cat when I went on a hiking trip, back when I actually did things—and she found me just sitting on the floor in the hallway. I hadn't moved in hours. And... she said I was just rocking back and forth, and I was saying it out loud. Over and over. I was just repeating, "I can't keep living like this, I can't keep living like this." I didn't even realize I was saying it until she grabbed my shoulders and shook me. It just... it spilled out of me because it's true. I really don't think I can keep living like this. It hurts too much, even though it's just emptiness, it somehow hurts so much, and I just want it to stop. I just want to go to sleep and never, ever have to wake up and feel this way again.
Have you ever heard voices or seen things that aren't there when you're alone?

Well... yeah. Yes, I do. It's... it's really hard to talk about because I know how it sounds, you know? I know it sounds crazy, but it's so real to me. It's... it's a woman's voice. And it always comes from the exact same spot, right in the corner of my bedroom, near where the window meets the closet. I'll just be lying there in bed, staring at the ceiling, feeling that heavy emptiness I was telling you about, and then... she'll just start talking. 

It's not like a thought in my head, it's not like my internal monologue. It's an actual, physical sound, as clear and loud as if you were standing right next to my bed right now, speaking to me. And she... she says these awful things. She tells me that I've ruined everything. That I've completely destroyed my life, that I've driven all my friends away—like Sarah, and the board game group—and that I'm a failure because I didn't go to that watercolor class, because I haven't painted in over a year. She just lists all my failures, over and over, and she tells me that I need to stay inside. She says, "You can't go out there, you'll just ruin that too, you need to stay in this room where you belong." 

And it's terrifying because I can't make her stop. I've tried putting in headphones, turning the AC up louder, burying my head under the pillows, but she just cuts right through all of it. Sometimes she talks for just a few minutes, but other times it feels like she goes on for hours, just this relentless, clear voice coming from the shadows in the corner, telling me how useless I am and how I have to stay hidden away. It's gotten to the point where I'm scared to even look in that corner of the room, even during the day, because I just know she's there, waiting to start again. It makes the emptiness feel so much worse, because even when I'm completely alone and isolated, I'm still being punished, you know? It's just... it's so loud, and I can't escape it.
Does the voice you hear ever tell you to do things, or is it only criticizing you?

Well... she mostly just criticizes me, like I said. It's... it's not like she's giving me commands to, you know, go out and do something specific, or... or hurt someone, or anything like that. It's more like she's just dictating my reality, if that makes sense? Like, she's not saying, "Go lock the door," she's saying, "You ruined everything, you have to stay inside." 

And it's just... it's so specific to that one spot. That corner where the window meets the closet. I'll just be lying there, and it's always a woman's voice. Always the same woman. And she just starts in on me. She tells me how I've completely destroyed my life, how I've ruined every good thing I ever had. And she tells me I need to stay inside. She says it over and over, that I should stay inside, that I belong in this room, hidden away because I'm such a disaster. 

And I know I already told you this, but I just... I really need you to understand how real it sounds. It's not an echo, it's not a memory of someone who was mean to me once. It sounds as clear... as absolutely, undeniably clear as someone standing right next to my bed. Like if you were standing there right now, talking to me, that's exactly what it sounds like. It has volume, it has tone, it has... presence. It fills the room. Even when I try to block it out, even when I pull the blankets over my ears or try to hum to myself, she's just right there, telling me I ruined everything and that I can never leave that room. It's just... it's so exhausting to be trapped with her.
Do you ever find it hard to follow your own thoughts or to express them in a way that makes sense to others?

Yeah... yes, actually. It's... it's really frustrating. It's like my brain is a radio scanning through stations way too fast, and I can't get it to stop on just one. Like, I'll be trying to explain to someone—maybe Sarah, or even just trying to write down what's been happening to me—and I'll start off making sense, I think. I'll start talking about... well, the divorce papers. They've just been sitting there on the kitchen island for I don't even know how long, just this thick stack of heavy, official paper that I can't bring myself to deal with. 

And then, while I'm trying to talk about the papers and how heavy they feel, I'll notice the color of them, this stark, blinding white, and suddenly my brain just completely shifts to paint colors. Because I used to paint, you know, with the watercolors before I stopped going to the class, and I'll start talking about titanium white and how it mixes with ultramarine, and how the colors just bleed into the texture of the canvas... and then, before I even realize I've changed the subject again, I'm suddenly obsessing over the number seven. I don't even know why it's seven, maybe it's because there were seven pages in the first section of the legal packet, or... or just the sharp shape of the number itself, but I'll just start talking about seven and how important it is. 

And it feels connected in my head! It feels like it all makes perfect, logical sense in that exact split second. But then I look at whoever I'm talking to, and they just have this blank, worried look on their face. Sarah does it a lot. She'll just gently put her hand on my arm, or she'll kind of interrupt me, and people keep telling me that they can't follow what I'm saying. They say, "I'm sorry, I lost you, what does the number seven have to do with the divorce papers or the paint?" And I can't explain it to them because by the time they ask, the connection is gone, the thought has vanished, and I'm just left feeling stupid and even more isolated. It's like I'm trapped behind this thick glass wall, and even when I try to reach out and explain what's happening to me, it just comes out as a tangled mess of random words. It just makes me not want to try talking at all, because what's the point if no one can follow my thoughts anyway?
Do you often find yourself jumping from one idea to another when talking or thinking?

Yeah, exactly. That's exactly what I was just trying to explain. It happens all the time, just like I was saying. I'll be genuinely trying to explain what's been happening to me, trying to get the words out about those divorce papers on the kitchen island, and how heavy and impossible they feel... and then my thoughts just completely jump. 

It's like my brain doesn't have any brakes. I go straight from the stark white of those legal documents to the titanium white paint colors I used to use, thinking about how I used to mix it with just a tiny drop of ultramarine to make the perfect sky color for these landscapes I used to do before everything got so dark. And then, before I can even finish my sentence about the paint, I'm suddenly fixated on the number seven. And in my head, it's this perfect, seamless bridge from one thought to the next! It makes complete, absolute sense why we went from the divorce papers to the paint to the sharp angle of a seven. 

But when I actually open my mouth and say the words out loud, people just... they look at me like I'm speaking a foreign language. They keep telling me they can't follow what I'm saying. Sarah does it constantly, she'll just stop me and say, "Wait, how did we get to watercolors?" And I get so incredibly frustrated because to me, we didn't jump, we just walked down the logical path! But to everyone else, I'm just bouncing around like a pinball. It's exhausting, honestly. I try so hard to keep track of where I started and where I ended up, but no matter how hard I try to explain it, nobody is ever going to understand the connections I'm making. It just makes me want to stop talking altogether, you know? Why even try to communicate if every time I try to explain what's happening, I just end up confusing everyone and feeling even more alone?
Do you find it difficult to stay focused on one topic when speaking or thinking?

Yes, I mean... isn't that what I just said? It's exactly that. It's incredibly difficult to stay focused on just one single topic. I try, I really do try to just stick to one thing, but it's like I have absolutely no control over the steering wheel in my own head. 

Like I keep trying to explain to you, I'll start off trying to talk about what's been happening, trying to focus on those divorce papers sitting right there on the counter, but my focus just... it just completely dissolves. One second I'm focused on the legal packet, and the next second my thoughts have completely jumped to paint colors, and then to the number seven, just like I was telling you. I can't keep my mind tethered to the original point no matter how hard I concentrate. It's like trying to hold water in my bare hands. 

And the absolute worst part is, I don't even realize I've lost focus until I look up and see the other person's face. People just keep telling me they can't follow what I'm saying. They say I'm all over the place, that I'm losing the thread of the conversation. But I'm not doing it on purpose! I want to just have a normal, straightforward conversation where I stay on track, but my brain just drags me away to these other things, and I can't stop it. It's just so exhausting trying to force my brain to walk in a straight line when it just wants to sprint in every possible direction at once.
Have you ever experienced a period of time where you felt abnormally happy, energetic, or irritable, and this feeling lasted for several days or longer?

Abnormally happy? No... no, definitely not. I don't... I can't even remember the last time I felt just normally happy, to be completely honest with you. The idea of being abnormally happy or having all this extra energy just sounds completely alien to me right now. It's actually the exact opposite. It's just this... this crushing, suffocating weight all the time. 

Like I was saying earlier about those divorce papers on the kitchen island, just looking at them drains whatever tiny bit of life I have left in me. Energetic? I mean, getting out of bed in the morning feels like I'm trying to walk through waist-deep wet cement. I don't have the energy to do anything at all. I used to have energy, you know, back when I was taking those watercolor classes and actually doing things, setting up my easel and mixing the paints, but now... I just sit there. I just sit and stare. I don't have these bursts where I'm suddenly cleaning the house or feeling on top of the world for days. Never. 

And irritable... I mean, I guess I get frustrated, like when Sarah interrupts me or when people look at me like I'm speaking a different language because they can't follow my thoughts, but it's not like I'm pacing around angry or keyed up. It's more just this deep, hollow, exhausting sadness that never, ever leaves. I honestly wish I had some energy, even if it was abnormal, because right now I just feel like I'm fading away into the couch cushions day after day, and I can't do anything to stop it. So, no, I haven't had anything like what you're describing. Just the heavy stuff.
Have you ever had a period where you felt extremely energetic or irritable and didn't need much sleep for several days?

Sleep? No, I... I sleep too much, if anything. I mean, going without sleep for days because I'm just so full of energy? That just doesn't happen to me. Like I was just saying, I don't get energetic. I don't have these periods where I'm wired and buzzing around the house. I'm just so tired all the time. 

I'll sleep for twelve, fourteen hours sometimes, and I still wake up feeling like I haven't slept at all. I just pull the covers back over my head because the thought of facing the day, of looking at the kitchen island and everything sitting on it... it's just too much. I'd rather just stay asleep. And even when I'm awake, I'm just sitting there, staring at the wall, feeling completely drained. I don't have the energy to be irritable in that keyed-up way you're talking about, where you're pacing and snapping at people because you just have so much restless energy and you haven't slept. I just don't have that in me. I'm just empty. 

So no, I've never had a time where I didn't need much sleep. I need all the sleep I can get, and even that's never enough to make me feel rested or give me any kind of energy. It's just a constant state of exhaustion. I wish I could just have one day where I woke up after eight hours and actually felt like getting out of bed, but that just never happens. It's just sleep, and then waking up tired, and then wanting to go back to sleep again.
Have you ever felt extremely energetic or unusually happy for several days in a row?

I feel like we're going in circles here... didn't you just ask me almost this exact same thing? About being abnormally happy or having all this energy? Because my answer hasn't changed in the last five minutes. No. I have never felt extremely energetic or unusually happy for days in a row. I don't think I've felt unusually happy for a single hour in a row, let alone days. 

Like I was just trying to explain to you, it's the exact opposite of that. I am just so incredibly tired and weighed down by absolutely everything. Just looking at the mail, looking at the kitchen counter with those divorce papers sitting there, it just sucks every last drop of life out of me. I don't have these magical days where I'm suddenly bouncing off the walls and feeling great. I really, really wish I did, because maybe then I could actually get something done, maybe I could finally pick up my watercolor brushes again instead of just letting them gather dust in the corner of the living room where I left them months ago. 

But no, it's just this constant, heavy, suffocating gray feeling. Every single day is exactly the same. There's no happiness, there's no sudden burst of energy. Just... nothing. I really don't understand why you keep asking me if I'm happy or energetic when I'm telling you I can barely even pull myself out from under the covers most mornings. It's just exhausting having to keep saying it. No, I don't get happy, and I don't get energetic. Ever.
Have you experienced any significant losses or traumatic events in the past year and a half, such as the loss of a loved one, a job, or a relationship?

Losses or traumatic events? In the past year and a half? I mean... no, not really. Not in the way you're asking. Nobody died, if that's what you mean. I haven't been to any funerals. My parents are still alive, they still live in the same house they've lived in since I was in high school, and my sister is still out in Colorado doing her thing. I haven't lost a job either, mostly because I haven't had a job to lose. I haven't worked in a long time, so there was no big dramatic firing or getting laid off or anything like that. I've just been at home. 

And as for relationships... I mean, I keep mentioning the divorce papers, but that's not... it didn't happen in the last year and a half. We separated way before that. The papers are just sitting there on the island, mocking me, but the actual loss of the marriage, the big blowup, the packing of the boxes and him driving away... that was years ago. It just feels like it's still happening because I can't bring myself to sign the papers and finalize it. It's like this agonizing, slow-motion thing that just drags on and on, but the actual event itself isn't recent. 

I haven't been in any accidents, my house hasn't burned down, nothing like that. It's just been a very slow, very quiet fading away. There's no big inciting incident that I can point to and say, 'Ah, yes, that's when everything went wrong.' It's just this creeping fog that came in and never left. I don't go out enough to have anything traumatic happen to me. I just go from the bed to the couch, maybe to the kitchen if I can force myself to eat something, and back to the couch. You can't really have a traumatic event when you're just sitting perfectly still in your own living room, staring at the dust motes in the air. So, no. No big losses or traumas recently. Just the same old nothingness.
Have you ever felt unusually happy or extremely energetic for several days in a row at any point in your life?

I... I really don't know how many different ways I can say this to you. We literally just talked about this. Are you... is there a reason you keep asking me the exact same thing? Because it feels like you're not hearing me at all. You added "at any point in your life" this time, but that doesn't change the answer. No. Never. Not when I was twenty, not when I was in high school, not ever. 

Even before things got this bad, even before the marriage fell apart and those papers ended up on the kitchen island... I was never that person. I've never been the girl who wakes up ready to take on the world, smiling for days on end, buzzing with all this endless energy. I don't even know what that feels like. I remember when I was taking classes at the college years ago, I'd look at the other students buzzing around the campus, laughing and talking so fast, making all these plans, and I just felt like I was moving underwater compared to them. I was just trying to drag myself from one lecture to the next so I could go back to my room and sleep. 

I have always been tired. I have always felt heavy. There is no secret period of my life where I was suddenly this vibrant, energetic person for days in a row. It just doesn't exist. My baseline has never been happy. So please, I'm just so tired... can we please stop talking about me being happy and energetic? Because it's just reminding me of exactly what I'm not, and it takes so much energy just to keep answering the same question over and over when all I want to do is close my eyes. I don't have those days. I never have.
Have you ever had a period where your thoughts, feelings, or behaviors were so unusual or extreme that they interfered with your daily life?

Well, I mean... yes. Yes, absolutely. If you're asking if my daily life is interfered with, then yes, it's completely... it's just completely destroyed at this point. I don't even know if you can call what I do a "daily life" anymore. It's more like a daily existence. Just... enduring. 

I used to do these freelance art-education gigs, you know? Going into community centers, sometimes after-school programs, teaching kids how to mix watercolors or do basic sketching. I loved it. It was exhausting, but it was a good kind of exhausting. But I had to stop all of that. I just... I couldn't get out of bed to do it. The thought of standing in front of a group of kids, trying to smile, trying to explain color theory when my own head is just this loud, chaotic mess of... of voices and heaviness... I just couldn't. I'd stare at the emails asking if I was available for the spring session, and I'd just let them sit there until they stopped asking. 

And it's not just the work. I used to play in this recreational soccer league on Thursday nights. Nothing serious, just running around, getting some fresh air. I haven't been to a game in... I don't even know how long. Months. I missed all the community events I used to go to, the art fairs downtown, the farmers market on Saturday mornings... I just stopped going. I can't be around people. I can't handle the noise, the expectations, the feeling that everyone is looking at me and knowing that something is profoundly wrong with my brain. 

It's gotten so bad that my friend... my friend Sarah, she has to come over and check on me. Because if she doesn't, I just... I won't eat. I'll realize it's been two days and all I've had is a handful of dry cereal. And showering... God, showering feels like climbing a mountain. The effort it takes to turn on the water, to stand there, to wash my hair... it's just too much. I'll go a week without doing it, just sitting in the same clothes on the couch. Sarah comes over and basically forces me into the bathroom. She brings groceries because she knows I won't go to the store. She's essentially keeping me alive right now, because I'm just not reliably keeping myself safe or taking care of even the most basic human needs. So, yes, my thoughts and my feelings... whatever is happening in my head, it has completely taken over everything. There is no normal life left.
Have you ever had a period where you felt extremely energetic or unusually happy?

I... I honestly don't understand what is happening right now. Did you... did you lose your place on your notepad? Or is this some kind of test to see if my answers change? Because I... I swear we just went over this. Like, literally just a few minutes ago. I just told you about how my friend Sarah has to come over and physically force me into the bathroom to shower because I can't even summon the energy to turn on the faucet, and now you're back to asking if I'm extremely energetic? 

No. The answer is still no. It's going to be no if you ask me again in five minutes, too. I don't have periods of being unusually happy. I don't have energy. I mean, just... look at me. Look at how much effort it takes just to sit here in this chair and string these sentences together for you. My limbs feel like they're filled with wet sand. Every time I breathe it feels like a chore. If I had a period where I felt extremely energetic, don't you think I would have used it to, I don't know, wash my own hair? Or finally sign those divorce papers sitting on the kitchen island? Or go back to teaching those kids how to paint? 

But I haven't done any of that. Because that energy doesn't exist in me. It's like you're asking a... a stone if it ever feels like flying. It just doesn't happen. I'm just heavy, all the time, every single day, and it takes everything I have just to endure it. So please, I am just... I am begging you, can we stop asking if I'm happy and energetic? Because I don't know what else I can possibly say to convince you that I am completely, utterly empty of whatever it is you're looking for.
Can you describe any times when you felt better, even if it was just for a short while, since this heaviness started?

Better... I mean, I guess it depends on what you mean by better. If you mean was I always this completely incapable of getting off the couch, then... no. There was a stretch, right before the absolute worst of this... this crushing heaviness really set in, where I guess I looked like I was doing better. I could still cook sometimes. Not anything elaborate, you know, but I could stand at the stove and boil water for pasta, maybe stir in some jarred sauce without feeling like I was going to physically collapse from the effort. And I was still answering my friends. When Sarah would text me, I'd actually pick up the phone and type out a reply instead of just staring at the screen until it went dark. So, on the outside, I was functioning. I was moving around.

But... it wasn't really better. Because even during those weeks when I was still cooking and texting, I was already... things were already really wrong in my head. I was already hearing the voice. It was just there, constantly, while I was trying to make dinner or fold a shirt or whatever. And the lights... the lights in the hallway outside my apartment... I had already spent weeks believing that they were signals. The way they flickered or buzzed when I opened my door, I just knew, I absolutely believed they were signals specifically about me. Like they were trying to tell me something, or someone was using them to monitor me. I'd stand there in my kitchen, stirring my stupid pasta, just listening to the voice and obsessing over what the hallway lights were trying to communicate about me. 

So I might have been up and walking around, but my mind was already completely caught up in all of that. It's like the voice and the signals were just... wearing me down, draining whatever battery I had left, until the depression finally just swept in and took over completely. So, no, I wouldn't call it feeling better. I was just upright while it was happening.
Have you ever had a period where your thoughts and feelings seemed completely disconnected from reality?

Disconnected from reality... see, that’s where I get stuck with these questions. Because what does that even mean? If something is happening right in front of you, over and over, it is your reality, isn't it? I mean, I know... I know it sounds impossible. I’m not stupid, I know exactly how it sounds to sit here in a doctor's office and say this out loud. But I am sure of it. 

I am absolutely, one hundred percent sure that the people living in the apartment downstairs—and I think they’re working with some of my ex’s friends, because his friends always hated me and they were always just so overly involved in everyone's business anyway—they have been tracking when I leave. They’re keeping tabs on my movements. And they know I'm going to leave before I even do anything. 

It’s the lights. I told you about the lights in the hallway earlier, right? How they're signals? Well, it's not just random signaling. It’s a tracking system. Because I will be sitting in my living room, just staring at the wall, and I’ll finally think to myself, "Okay, I need to go to the store. I have to go get some juice or whatever." doctor.question: Have you ever had a period where your thoughts, feelings, or behaviors were so unusual or extreme that they interfered with your daily life?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: I’ve stopped taking freelance art-education work, missed community events and soccer, and I need my friend checking on me because I’m not reliably eating, showering, or keeping myself safe.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the patient's symptoms (unusual thoughts, feelings, or behaviors) have interfered with their daily life, which corresponds to functional impairment.

patient.answer:
Well, I mean... yes. Yes, absolutely. If you're asking if my daily life is interfered with, then yes, it's completely... it's just completely destroyed at this point. I don't even know if you can call what I do a "daily life" anymore. It's more like a daily existence. Just... enduring. 

I used to do these freelance art-education gigs, you know? Going into community centers, sometimes after-school programs, teaching kids how to mix watercolors or do basic sketching. I loved it. It was exhausting, but it was a good kind of exhausting. But I had to stop all of that. I just... I couldn't get out of bed to do it. The thought of standing in front of a group of kids, trying to smile, trying to explain color theory when my own head is just this loud, chaotic mess of... of voices and heaviness... I just couldn't. I'd stare at the emails asking if I was available for the spring session, and I'd just let them sit there until they stopped asking. 

And it's not just the work. I used to play in this recreational soccer league on Thursday nights. Nothing serious, just running around, getting some fresh air. I haven't been to a game in... I don't even know how long. Months. I missed all the community events I used to go to, the art fairs downtown, the farmers market on Saturday mornings... I just stopped going. I can't be around people. I can't handle the noise, the expectations, the feeling that everyone is looking at me and knowing that something is profoundly wrong with my brain. 

It's gotten so bad that my friend... my friend Sarah, she has to come over and check on me. Because if she doesn't, I just... I won't eat. I'll realize it's been two days and all I've had is a handful of dry cereal. And showering... God, showering feels like climbing a mountain. The effort it takes to turn on the water, to stand there, to wash my hair... it's just too much. I'll go a week without doing it, just sitting in the same clothes on the couch. Sarah comes over and basically forces me into the bathroom. She brings groceries because she knows I won't go to the store. She's essentially keeping me alive right now, because I'm just not reliably keeping myself safe or taking care of even the most basic human needs. So, yes, my thoughts and my feelings... whatever is happening in my head, it has completely taken over everything. There is no normal life left.

patient.answer:
Better... I mean, I guess it depends on what you mean by better. If you mean was I always this completely incapable of getting off the couch, then... no. There was a stretch, right before the absolute worst of this... this crushing heaviness really set in, where I guess I looked like I was doing better. I could still cook sometimes. Not anything elaborate, you know, but I could stand at the stove and boil water for pasta, maybe stir in some jarred sauce without feeling like I was going to physically collapse from the effort. And I was still answering my friends. When Sarah would text me, I'd actually pick up the phone and type out a reply instead of just staring at the screen until it went dark. So, on the outside, I was functioning. I was moving around.

But... it wasn't really better. Because even during those weeks when I was still cooking and texting, I was already... things were already really wrong in my head. I was already hearing the voice. It was just there, constantly, while I was trying to make dinner or fold a shirt or whatever. And the lights... the lights in the hallway outside my apartment... I had already spent weeks believing that they were signals. The way they flickered or buzzed when I opened my door, I just knew, I absolutely believed they were signals specifically about me. Like they were trying to tell me something, or someone was using them to monitor me. I'd stand there in my kitchen, stirring my stupid pasta, just listening to the voice and obsessing over what the hallway lights were trying to communicate about me. 

So I might have been up and walking around, but my mind was already completely caught up in all of that. It's like the voice and the signals were just... wearing me down, draining whatever battery I had left, until the depression finally just swept in and took over completely. So, no, I wouldn't call it feeling better. I was just upright while it was happening.

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I know it sounds impossible, but I’m sure the people downstairs and some of my ex’s friends have been tracking when I leave, because the hallway lights blink right after I think about going to the store.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking a general screening question for psychosis (losing touch with reality), which directly relates to the patient's delusions and fixed false beliefs about being tracked.

patient.answer:
Disconnected from reality... see, that’s where I get stuck with these questions. Because what does that even mean? If something is happening right in front of you, over and over, it is your reality, isn't it? I mean, I know... I know it sounds impossible. I’m not stupid, I know exactly how it sounds to sit here in a doctor's office and say this out loud. But I am sure of it. 

I am absolutely, one hundred percent sure that the people living in the apartment downstairs—and I think they’re working with some of my ex’s friends, because his friends always hated me and they were always just so overly involved in everyone's business anyway—they have been tracking when I leave. They’re keeping tabs on my movements. And they know I'm going to leave before I even do anything. 

It’s the lights. I told you about the lights in the hallway earlier, right? How they're signals? Well, it's not just random signaling. It’s a tracking system. Because I will be sitting in my living room, just staring at the wall, and I’ll finally think to myself, "Okay, I need to go to the store. I have to go get some juice or whatever." I won't say it out loud. I won't put my shoes on. I won't even grab my keys. I literally just *think* about going to the store. And right then... *blink*. The hallway lights blink. Right at that exact second. Every single time. 

It’s like they’re tapped into my head, monitoring when I’m about to cross the threshold of my own front door. They're letting each other know I'm about to move. So, you might call that disconnected from reality, or you might write down that I'm crazy, but when you’re the one sitting alone in a silent room and the light outside your door blinks the very second you think about walking to the grocery store... it's the most real thing in the world. It’s terrifying, is what it is. How can I possibly leave my apartment when they're tracking my thoughts like that?

patient.answer:
I... I don't know how to answer the part about knowing it is not real. Because when it happens, it doesn't feel like a trick of the mind. It feels... it just feels like it is happening. I mentioned the voice earlier, when you were asking about when I could still make pasta. It is... it is a woman’s voice. And she is always, always in the exact same spot. 

My bedroom has this one corner, right over by where the window meets the closet. I spend a lot of time in bed now, obviously, because of the heaviness, so I am just lying there for hours, staring at that corner. And that is where she speaks from. It is not like a thought in my head, you have to understand that. It is not my own internal monologue telling me things, it is an actual, physical sound in the room. It sounds as clear as someone standing right next to my bed. Like... like if you were standing here right now and leaned over to speak to me, that is exactly how clear and loud it is. 

She just talks to me from that corner. She tells me that I ruined everything. Over and over. Just saying I ruined everything. And maybe she is right, I mean, look at my life, look at the divorce papers I mentioned earlier, but having someone stand there and say it out loud to you while you cannot even sit up... it is unbearable. And she tells me I should stay inside. That I need to stay inside the apartment. Which, you know, with the lights in the hallway and the neighbors tracking me, it almost feels like she is warning me, or maybe she is part of it, I really do not know. I just know that she wants me to stay exactly where I am. 

And you ask if I know it is not real... I mean, logically, I locked the deadbolt. I know I live alone. I know there shouldn't be a woman in my bedroom. But when you hear the actual breath behind the words, when you can hear the tone of her voice echoing in the space... how do you convince yourself that is not real? I will pull the blankets over my head, just trying to block her out, but it doesn't matter because she sounds so close. She just keeps telling me I ruined it all, and I just lie there and listen to her because... well, what else can I do? I can't leave. She says to stay inside, and the lights are waiting for me outside, so I just... I just stay in bed and listen to her.
